evidence: RULE 1: a MEASURED offset must exist as its OWN ROW. Recording a measurement inside another row's evidence prose does not reach the resolver. Rows starting with # are skipped by jlc_rotation_resolve.py.

RULE 2 (2026-07-25, THE CORRECTION BELOW): NEVER populate a row from jlc_twin's jlc_offset. Derive it from the BOARD + JLC's cached model with an operator VERIFIED against pcbnew itself (pad.GetFPRelativePosition() vs pad.GetPosition()). jlc_twin.xform() used the wrong handedness, so every offset it reported was NEGATED: invisible at 0/180 (sign-invariant) and exactly 180deg wrong at 90/270. Six rows here were populated from it and were all 180deg wrong. Checker and checked must not share a method (canon M1).

RULE 3 (2026-07-25, canon A-POL): the `polarity` column is a REQUIRED DECLARATION, one of n/a | two-channel | single-channel. A pad-NUMBER fit structurally CANNOT detect a model whose own numbering differs from ours, and a HIGH FIT MARGIN IS NOT CONFIDENCE: on usb-hub-3s-v3's indicator LEDs (C2296/C2297) the pad-number fit returns 180 with a 17.7x margin and is WRONG — JLC numbers pad 1 = ANODE while KiCad Device:LED is pin 1 = K, both libraries draw the cathode WEST, so the true offset is 0 and a 180 row would ship every indicator dark (indistinguishable from a bad joint). two-channel = a NUMBERING-FREE channel (silk chamfer, pin-1 dot/glyph, mounting-tab position, body/courtyard asymmetry, lead axis) is RECORDED IN THIS ROW. single-channel = no such channel exists; the row MUST name the JLC order-preview human gate, which then carries it before first order. Graded by jlc_rotation_audit.py --table.

Indicator LED 0603 (POLARIZED); pluto-rx2-8way-v2 LED_ST. Measured 2026-07-30 BY HAND from the raw .kicad_mod text of both lands -- own parser, own operator, no pcbnew and no import of jlc_rotation_measure.py, which WITHHELD this code (canon M1). THE PAD-NUMBER FIT IS CONFIDENTLY WRONG HERE AND THE CHANNELS DISAGREE: it returns 180 at rms 0.0375mm vs 1.0875mm next best (29x) purely because the two libraries number the terminals oppositely -- our KiCad LED_SMD:LED_0603_1608Metric puts pad 1 at x=-0.7875 (WEST) while JLC's LED-SMD_L1.6-W0.8-R-RD puts pad 1 at x=+0.7500 (EAST). The PAD CLOUD is DEGENERATE: rms 0.0375mm at BOTH 0 and 180, and 1.0875mm at 90/270, because a 2-pad chip land is its own 180 reflection (measured: each land's own pad set maps onto itself at 180). Geometry therefore admits {0,180} and only a polarity mark can choose between them. NUMBERING-FREE CHANNEL, marks read as SHAPES. OURS: the F.SilkS bracket's closed full-height edge is at x=-1.485 and the F.Fab body chamfer cuts the (-0.800,-0.400) corner, both on the -x end; and the BOARD says the same thing without reading any drawing, because LED_ST pad 1 is on GND while pad 2 is on LED_STAT_A -- our pad 1 IS the cathode (KiCad Device:LED pin 1 = K). JLC: their land carries TWO DISTINCT asymmetric marks at OPPOSITE ends -- a pin-1 DOT (F.SilkS circle r=0.050 at (+0.80,-0.40), beside their pad 1 at x=+0.75) and a CHAMFERED silk bracket at the far -x end (corners (-1.40,-0.70)->(-1.70,-0.40) and (-1.70,+0.40)->(-1.40,+0.70)). A pin-1 dot already marks pin 1, so the chamfer marks the other thing an LED land has to mark, the CATHODE; and their diode glyph corroborates it with no pad number read, the full-height cathode BAR sitting at x=+0.090 with its lead running WEST to x=-0.120. So JLC's cathode is the -x end = THEIR PAD 2, i.e. JLC numbers pad 1 = ANODE. BOTH LIBRARIES DRAW THE CATHODE WEST => the physical parts already align => offset 0. THE TWIN'S ROT-DB-SUGGEST LINE PROPOSING 'add LCSC row C2286,180' IS WRONG, and it is recorded here because a machine proposal that would brick a board is exactly what this row exists to document. That line reports the fitted jlc_offset, which on this part measures a LABELLING difference and not a geometric one; the twin's own POLARITY-FIT line in the SAME report file says the marking channel disagrees by 180 and that offset 0 is what places the part correctly, so one artifact states both answers and only the wrong one is phrased as a paste-ready row. A 180 row would seat every unit with its cathode east onto a west cathode pad: reverse-biased, dark, and indistinguishable from a bad solder joint -- the C2296/C2297 outcome, on the only status indicator this board has. Because the two channels disagreed, LED_ST goes on the JLC ORDER-PREVIEW human gate before the first order.

Kinghelm KH-SMA-KE-Z vertical THT SMA flange jack; pluto-rx2-8way-v2 J_ANT1-J_ANT8, J_RX1, J_RX2 -- 10 placements, every RF port on the board. Measured 2026-07-30 BY HAND from the raw .kicad_mod text of both lands -- own parser, own operator, no pcbnew, a DIFFERENT method from jlc_rotation_measure.py, which withheld this code (canon M1). THE PAD-NUMBER FIT IS USELESS ON THIS PART AND MUST NOT BE READ AS A MARGIN: rms 3.9350mm at 0, 4.5437mm at 90, 5.0800mm at 180, 4.5437mm at 270 -- every angle is garbage, because the two libraries number DIFFERENT PHYSICAL FEATURES. Ours numbers pad 1 = the CENTRE RF pin with pads 2-5 = the four ground posts; JLC numbers pad 5 = the centre with pads 1-4 = the posts. That is the C3020560 USB-C class, where a numbered fit pairs our signal pads against their shell posts. THE NUMBERING-FREE PAD CLOUD (pads grouped into size classes ranked by area, each of our pads matched to the nearest of the paired class, no pad number read) measures rms 0.0000mm at ALL FOUR ANGLES -- 1.0x, fully degenerate -- because the land is four posts on a 5.08mm square plus one pin on the axis, which is its own 90-degree rotation. WHAT DECIDES IT IS THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO DECIDE, and that is a measurement, made on three independent things. (1) PADS: our own land's pad set (positions and sizes, no numbers) maps onto itself at 90, 180 AND 270 degrees, and so does JLC's. (2) GRAPHICS: every graphic primitive of OUR land maps onto itself at 90, 180 and 270 as well -- the 6.5mm F.Fab body square, the F.Fab insulator circle on the origin, the four 0.9mm F.Fab post squares spanning 2.09..2.99mm in each quadrant, and the four F.SilkS corner brackets at +-3.900. Our land carries NO asymmetric feature of any kind, so there is no mark for a mark-to-mark channel to match and no orientation our own copper is able to express. JLC's land has exactly ONE asymmetric graphic, an F.SilkS pin-1 dot of r=0.030 at (-3.25,+3.25); a pin-1 dot FOLLOWS pad numbering so it is not admissible, and it has no counterpart on our side to be matched against in any case. (3) NETS: on the board, pad 1 of all ten refs carries the RF signal (ANT1-ANT7, RX1_MAIN, RX2_OUT) and sits ON the rotation axis, while pads 2-5 are all GND -- so a 90-degree turn permutes the ground posts among themselves and leaves the netlist IDENTICAL. All four candidate angles are therefore the SAME PHYSICAL PLACEMENT: the machine cannot misorient this part, and 0 is correct by measured symmetry rather than by fit. THIS ROW DOES NOT REQUIRE THE ORDER-PREVIEW HUMAN GATE -- a human at the preview would have nothing to confirm, and routing a part that has no orientation to a human gate is how a gate teaches its operators to wave rows through (the failure the C2762192 tool-gap note warns about). CONTRAST, on this same board, with C5121458, which is ALSO cloud-degenerate at all four angles and IS declared single-channel: there the degeneracy hides a real 90-degree error because its 24 pads carry 24 different nets. Here the degeneracy is the absence of the question.

pSemi PE42482A-X SP8T RF switch in QFN-24 4.0x4.0mm, 0.50mm pitch, centred 2.7mm exposed pad; pluto-rx2-8way-v2 U_SW -- the eight-way antenna switch, i.e. the board's whole signal function. Measured 2026-07-30 BY HAND from the raw .kicad_mod text of both lands -- own parser, own operator, no pcbnew, a DIFFERENT method from jlc_rotation_measure.py, which withheld this code (canon M1). PAD-NUMBER fit over the 25 common pad numbers (our nine 0.75mm paste sub-apertures share number 25 with the exposed pad, so that number is reduced to its centroid, which is the origin on both sides): offset 0 at rms 0.0098mm, vs 2.8927mm at 90 AND at 270 and 4.0909mm at 180 -- next-best separation 295x. DECLARED single-channel: no numbering-free channel exists, and unusually for this table the degeneracy is FOURFOLD rather than the customary 0-vs-180. The PAD CLOUD (size classes ranked by area and paired by rank, paste sub-apertures dropped as pads wholly contained inside a larger pad, no pad number read) measures rms 0.0098mm at ALL FOUR ANGLES -- 1.0x, no discrimination whatever -- because six pads per side on a four-sided land with a centred square exposed pad is its own 90-degree rotation; our own land's pad set maps onto itself at 90, 180 and 270, and so does JLC's. The only asymmetric graphics on either side are PIN-1 MARKS: ours an F.Fab corner chamfer (-2.00,-1.70)->(-1.70,-2.00) plus an F.Fab circle at (-1.55,-1.55) and an F.SilkS dot at (-2.95,-2.60); JLC's an F.SilkS dot at (-2.00,-2.00), a Cmts.User circle at (-1.78,-1.27) and a filled F.SilkS corner triangle. A pin-1 mark FOLLOWS pad numbering, so it cannot corroborate a pad-NUMBER fit. A 295x margin is NOT confidence about numbering -- canon A-POL exists because C2296 returns 17.7x and is wrong, and C2286 on THIS BOARD is a live instance of exactly that. Per RULE 3 this row MUST be carried by the JLC ORDER-PREVIEW HUMAN GATE before the first order (the C13755 precedent: a 543x fit that still bought a human eye). NOTE the advisory footprint-NAME DB rule for the QFN-16/20/24/28/40 family would have said 270, which is 90 degrees off this measurement -- not the 180 handedness signature, so it is an ordinary wrong name rule of the partial-prefix kind and the MEASUREMENT wins. Ninety degrees out would rotate all 24 pins around the die: every antenna port, the four control lines and the RF common land on the wrong pin, which on an SP8T is not a degraded board but a dead one.
